rows.behavior: kmctl verify ID --by human:ID appends a verified entry with today's date to an unverified .okf/ concept, appends a line to .okf/log.md, and kmctl review due no longer lists that id.
rows.fails_when: the concept still appears in kmctl review due after the verb exits 0, the entry lacks by or at, or log.md gains no line naming the concept

rows.behavior: kmctl verify takes a docs/ page id as kmctl review due prints it and writes the entry into that page's front matter.
rows.fails_when: a docs page id is refused, or the page's front matter has no verified entry afterwards

rows.behavior: kmctl verify changes only the verified list: every other line of the file stays byte for byte, and an existing verified list keeps its entries with the new one appended.
rows.fails_when: any line outside the verified list differs, or an earlier verified entry is lost or reordered

rows.behavior: kmctl verify refuses, with one line on stderr naming the fix and exit 1, when --by does not start with human:, the id matches no file, the id is a handoff, or the front matter cannot be read; it writes nothing then.
rows.fails_when: any of those cases exits 0, prints the refusal on stdout, gives no fix, or changes a file

rows.behavior: kmctl verify --json prints one JSON object with id, path, by and at; the text output ends with a Next: kmctl review due line.
rows.fails_when: the JSON lacks a key or is not one object, or the text output has no Next: line naming kmctl review due

rows.behavior: kmctl review due's text output ends with a Next: line naming kmctl verify when it lists anything due, prints no such line when nothing is due, and its --json output keeps its keys; the briefing tests still pass under TOKEN_BUDGET.
rows.fails_when: the due listing lacks a Next: line naming kmctl verify, the nothing-due output has one, the JSON gains or loses a key, or a briefing test fails

rows.behavior: The audit skill and both okf-bundle rules (Claude and Antigravity) name kmctl verify and say an agent runs it only after the named person confirmed the concept.
rows.fails_when: any of the three files does not mention kmctl verify

rows.behavior: kmctl verify --help passes the repository's help tests: one-line docstring, an example for every input, renders at 80 columns.

A new ADR records that kmctl verify writes a person's check and an agent may run it only on that person's confirmation, without changing ADR 0005 or I2; docs/reference/commands.md and the architecture overview's Depicts list name the verb.
rows.fails_when: no ADR covers the verb, the wording lets an audit verdict alone trigger it, or the reference or Depicts list omits it

rows.behavior: The full lint and test gates pass, including the APM package body-hash test the rule edit changes.
rows.fails_when: just lint or just test exits nonzero
